svg.title: Global climate context: warming, emissions, sea level and recorded floods
svg.desc: Four charts. Global mean temperature anomaly rising to plus 1.53 degrees Celsius in 2024, with strong El Nino years marked. Global fossil carbon dioxide emissions reaching 38.6 billion tonnes in 2024. Global mean sea level up about 218 millimetres since 1900. Recorded flood disasters averaging 171 per year over 2015 to 2024, against 26 per year in the 1970s.
svg.text: A warming world, and more water
Global context for a local question. Every series below is downloaded from its publisher, not estimated; sources are named on each panel.
Dashed vertical rules on the temperature panel mark strong El Niño years (peak Niño 3.4 anomaly ≥ +1.5 °C, NOAA CPC) — they ride on top of the trend rather than causing it.
“Recorded” is doing real work in the flood panel: reporting improved through the century, so part of that rise is better record-keeping rather than more water.
